stories.notes: Story has empty acceptance criteria and null spec — requires full elaboration from scratch. 'Live Preview of Content in CMS' is a complex feature spanning multiple workspaces (GO, UP, MX) involving real-time rendering and content management. Assigning both agents: openspec first to define AC and add technical depth, then speckit to harden with testability, security, and edge-case coverage.

agentContributions.notes: Novel capability — Live Preview does not exist in the codebase. The attachment point is useContent, the central hook (236 callers) through which every Contentstack component fetches content. Live Preview must plug into this layer so that content changes from the CMS are reflected in the rendered UI without a full page reload. VCs are derived solely from the description since ACs are empty. Contentstack is an unreachable external service at test time, so VCs are framed at our code boundary with mocked responses.

Openspec provided empty acceptanceCriteria, so all 12 ACs are new. I derived them from the story title (Live Preview of Content in CMS), the description, and the listed files (useContent.ts as the integration point, contentstack.ts as the service layer, contentCard.ts and ContentstackLink.tsx as consuming components). Key design decisions: (1) AC-1/AC-2 establish the happy path and graceful degradation baseline; (2) AC-3/AC-4 cover reconnection resilience; (3) AC-5 addresses security by ensuring Live Preview never activates in production; (4) AC-6 covers accessibility for dynamic content updates per WCAG live-region requirements; (5) AC-7 ensures consistency across multiple consumers of the same entry via useContent (236 callers); (6) AC-8 handles malformed data edge case; (7) AC-9 protects user interaction state during updates; (8) AC-10 ensures cleanup on unmount; (9) AC-11 specifically validates the ContentstackLink component path listed in technical notes; (10) AC-12 addresses rapid-update coalescing. All ACs are framed as observable outcomes at the code boundary since Contentstack is an unreachable external service at test time. I could not review the actual file contents, so ACs are based on file paths and naming conventions — if useContent.ts has existing caching, polling, or error-handling patterns, some ACs may need adjustment.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: OpenSpec performed analysis (identifying useContent as the attachment point, noting 236 callers, framing VCs at code boundary) but did not actually produce acceptance criteria — acceptanceChanged is false and splitCount is 0. This is a failure of OpenSpec's primary deliverable. SpecKit compensated by deriving all 12 ACs from scratch using only the story title, description, and file paths. While SpecKit's ACs are well-structured (covering happy path, graceful degradation, reconnection resilience, production security guard, WCAG live-region accessibility, multi-consumer consistency, malformed data, interaction-state preservation, cleanup on unmount, component-specific validation, and rapid-update coalescing), SpecKit explicitly notes it could not review actual file contents. ACs were written blind based on naming conventions, not existing caching/polling/error-handling patterns in useContent.ts. The two agents did not add non-overlapping value in the intended pipeline order — OpenSpec's contribution was analysis-only with no AC output, and SpecKit had to do both elaboration and review simultaneously. Human review is required to validate the 12 ACs against the actual codebase, confirm they align with existing patterns in useContent.ts and contentstack.ts, and verify that the security AC (no production activation) matches the actual environment-detection mechanism used in the codebase.
